# Bram Peulers — Product designer & facilitator

> Freelance product designer and facilitator based in the Netherlands. He takes teams and decision-makers from an idea to a tested prototype, using AI to make ideas tangible fast and validating with real users. 10+ years of product design. Domain experience in energy (home base: Essent, Eneco), finance, insurance, healthcare, e-commerce and retail. Available for short sprints and long-term engagements (e.g. a year), embedded in one or more teams. The site is available in Dutch (default) and English.

## Services
- Product design: end-to-end UX and UI for apps, websites and portals, built on scalable design systems and tested with real users.
- UX design: user research, customer needs and interaction design.
- Service design: the full customer journey across channels, including processes and systems behind it.
- From idea to prototype: a clickable prototype tested with real users within a few weeks, using AI prototyping.
- Facilitation & AI products: workshops towards shared decisions; designing trust, errors and control into AI features.

## Articles
- [From Figma to AI prototype: testing faster with real customers](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/prototype-figma-ai/): A step-by-step plan for turning a Figma design into a working prototype with Claude, and testing it with real customers. Using the Essent prototype as an example.
- [Five prompts to bring a Figma design to life](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/prompts-figma-prototype/): Concrete prompts for turning a static Figma design into a working prototype with AI, ready for testing.
- [Designing AI features: trust, explanation and control](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/ai-functies-ontwerpen/): How do you design AI features that users understand, trust and can steer themselves? Three principles and practical design patterns.
- [When an AI prototype is not the best choice](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/wanneer-geen-ai-prototype/): AI prototypes are powerful, but not always the right step. When you’re better off sketching, staying in Figma or building straight away.
- [Usability testing with 8 customers: getting the most out of it](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/usability-testen-8-klanten/): With eight participants you find the key problems and see patterns. How to prepare the test, run it and process the results.
- [From test insight to decision: getting decision-makers on board](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/van-testinzicht-naar-besluit/): Research only matters when it leads to a decision. How to present findings so product owners and management can act on them straight away.
- [Working within an existing design system as a freelancer](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/design-system-als-freelancer/): As a freelancer you often join an organisation with its own design system. How to become productive quickly, stay consistent and still add value.
- [Multi-brand design: one flow, different identities](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/multi-brand-design/): How do you design one solution that works for several brands, each with its own look? Lessons from working on a claims flow for Achmea.
- [The handover to development: avoiding surprises](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/overdracht-naar-development/): A good design can still go wrong during the build. How to ensure a smooth handover to development, without misunderstandings afterwards.
- [UX, UI or visual design: what are the differences?](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/ux-ui-visual-design/): The terms are often used interchangeably. A clear explanation of three different disciplines.
- [The benefits of a design system](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/design-system/): How a design system helps organisations keep their digital products consistent.
- [Why does a consistent brand identity matter?](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/huisstijl/): Recognisability builds trust. Why consistency pays off for every brand.
- [Smart navigation for higher conversion on your website](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/navigatie/): A clear navigation structure helps visitors find what they are looking for — and increases conversion.
- [How do you map a customer journey?](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/customer-journey/): A tutorial for making your customer’s journey visible before, during and after the purchase.
- [How do you develop a persona?](https://www.brampeulers.com/en/articles/persona/): How to put the customer truly at the centre of your project, with a persona as the starting point.
